# Worldview @ Stage 10 — Concrete Peak

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 66 to 140+ lines.

| Field | Value |

| IST Stage# | 10 |

## Expression on this line

Worldview at Order 8 is **framework-evaluation**: the agent can now step outside its own
worldview and evaluate it against alternative worldviews. "The scientific worldview
produces technological power but may miss subjective meaning. The spiritual worldview
produces meaning but may resist empirical testing. Which tradeoff is acceptable?" This
is the post-modern worldview insight: every worldview embodies values, and different
value systems produce different worldviews.

The key advance from Stage 9 is **worldview pluralism**. The agent no longer constructs
worldviews within a single framework — it evaluates multiple frameworks and recognizes
that each embodies different values.

Worldview at Stage 10 is understood as **value-laden**. The agent recognizes that
"objective" worldview is not a neutral concept — it presupposes that objectivity is the
right criterion, which is itself a value choice.

This framework-evaluation capacity opens up **genuine worldview pluralism**. The agent
can hold multiple worldview paradigms simultaneously without collapsing into relativism.

But worldview reasoning at Stage 10 is still **framework-dependent**. The agent evaluates
frameworks from within a meta-framework but cannot step outside that meta-framework.

The transition from Stage 10 to Stage 11 occurs when the agent can integrate multiple
worldview frameworks into a coherent meta-system.

In human development, Stage 10 corresponds to the thinker who can evaluate worldviews
across paradigms.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Cultural worldview pluralism becomes institutionalized.

- **UR:** The individual agent can evaluate worldviews from outside any particular
  framework.

- **LL:** Multi-paradigm worldview institutions emerge: interfaith dialogue centers,
  comparative philosophy departments, cross-cultural research institutes.

- **LR:** The comparative religion department, the philosophy of science journal, the
  cross-cultural psychology lab.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Paradigm paralysis — cannot commit to any worldview.

- **Dark allergy:** Framework fundamentalism — insists one worldview is superior.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to pluralism as an identity.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting pluralism as moral weakness.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Framework evaluation:** The agent can articulate value assumptions in worldviews.

- **Paradigm comparison:** The agent can compare worldviews across paradigms.

- **Value-aware worldview reasoning:** The agent recognizes that "objective" presupposes
  values.

- **Meta-framework dependency:** The agent evaluates from within a meta-framework but
  cannot evaluate the meta-framework.
